newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka troops advance slowly, fortify in north.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka troops advance slowly, fortify in north.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops were reported to be advancing slowly into northern rebel-held territory on Tuesday after facing fierce resistence earlier from Tamil Tiger guerrillas.

Military officials in the north said the army pounded rebel areas northeast of Omanthai on Monday with artillery and began advancing from Rambaikulam, which was captured in fierce weekend fighting from the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE).
"There was some fighting overnight. They (troops) are advancing," one military official said.
But a Defence Ministry statement said that troops spent most of Tuesday consolidating their positions in the freshly captured northern areas, building fortifications and organising supplies.
The Defence Ministry said 14 soldiers were killed and 19 wounded in the fighting at Rambaikulam. No casualties were reported on Monday.
The LTTE, meanwhile, hit back in the west on Tuesday. One officer and five soldiers were killed at Pesalai in Mannar when a tractor carrying troops hit a mine, military officials said.
Troops resumed their drive into the northern rebel heartland at the weekend after a five-day pause, but were slowed by fierce LTTE resistence. Several soldiers and rebels were killed.
The Defence Ministry said troops had moved three km (1.8 miles) north of Omanthai to Rambaikulam during the weekend.

Security forces captured Omanthai, 14 km (nine miles) north of the government-held town of Vavuniya, and Nedunkeni, 40 miles (25 km) northeast of Vavuniya, last week after a two-pronged thrust into the LTTE's northern Wanni heartland.
Vavuniya is 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo.
Casualty figures released by the Defence Ministry said 89 soldiers had died and about 145 had been wounded in the 14-day-old offensive, one of the military's biggest in the war.
Hospital sources said about 600 soldiers were wounded.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the ethnic war, now in its 14th year, but the LTTE say the toll is higher.
Some 20,000 troops launched "Operation Jaya Sikuru", or "Sure of Victory", from Vavuniya on May 13 in a bid to open a supply route to the Jaffna peninsula, 100 km (60 miles) further north.

The LTTE, fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in mainly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east, have accused Colombo of killing Tamil civilians and destroying their property under the pretext of opening a supply route.
Officials in Vavuniya said on Tuesday that the government had agreed to send food into the rebel-held Wanni region, where hundreds of people have been displaced by the offensive.

Fifty trucks of food and other essential items would be sent in daily. The military is working on a route to avoid the battle zone, the officials said, and food convoys were likely to start rolling out this week.
A statement from the LTTE's international secretariat in London on Tuesday accused the Sri Lankan government of launching a "food-siege" and said the refugee crisis was spiralling out of control.
